content.text:
The landing page is in `src/App.vue`, built only from `@eltonbautista/vue` components and `--cab-*` tokens, and `npm run build` passes. I haven't run it in a browser or tested it with a screen reader, so the keyboard and screen-reader behaviour is untested.

- **Title and intro:** one `<h1>` and a short intro paragraph.
- **Tracks:** Board games (`/tracks/board`), Digital (`/tracks/digital`) and Live-action (`/tracks/larp`) are `CabCard`s with `href`, so the whole card is clickable. Each card has one tab stop, a visible focus ring and the title as its link name. They sit in a list under an `<h2>`.
- **Sign-up form:** Name, Email and an Experience level select, plus a required code-of-conduct checkbox.
  - On submit, empty or invalid fields show an error message.
  - Focus moves to the first invalid field, which also covers the unchecked checkbox.
  - The form isn't submitted until it is valid.
  - The checkbox error goes through the checkbox's `hint` prop, because `CabCheckbox` doesn't pass attributes through to its `<input>`. This way screen readers still read the error with the checkbox.
- **Email reminders:** a `CabSwitch` that applies immediately, with no save button. It announces "Email reminders are on/off. Saved." through a live region. Nothing is actually saved: the switch only sets local state and shows the message, so you'll need to call a real endpoint there.
- **Booking confirmation:** a valid submit opens a `CabDialog` that summarises name, email and experience, with "Go back" and "Confirm booking". Confirming shows a "You're booked" message and moves focus to it. Escape or "Go back" cancels and returns focus to the Sign up button. No booking request is sent either, so that also needs wiring up.

The `/tracks/*` links are plain `href`s, so they only work once those routes exist on your side.
